subject: Chemistry
title: Wurtz Reaction: Join Two Alkyl Groups
summary: Alkyl halides react with sodium in dry ether to give alkanes with double the number of carbon atoms. In this lesson: 2RX + 2Na in dry ether gives R-R + 2NaX, bromomethane to ethane, how it works in a simple ionic picture (Na gives electrons, R- attacks a second R-X from the back, beyond NCERT), why two different halides give a mixture of three alkanes, why methane cannot be made, and two solved questions.

notes.title: Wurtz Reaction
notes.blurb: the reaction, how it works (a simple picture, beyond ncert), uses and limits, solved questions

keyPoints: **Wurtz reaction**: Two alkyl groups **join**. The number of carbons **doubles**.
**How it works**: A simple picture, **beyond NCERT**. R⁻ attacks from the **back**.
**Limitation**: Best for **symmetrical** alkanes. **Methane** cannot be made.

blocks.p: Examples: 2 CH₃Br + 2 Na → CH₃–CH₃ (ethane) + 2 NaBr; 2 CH₃CH₂Br + 2 Na → CH₃CH₂CH₂CH₃ (butane) + 2 NaBr.

sections.h: How it works (a simple picture, beyond NCERT)

list: Sodium is strongly electropositive. Two Na atoms each give one electron to R–X: R–X + 2 Na → R⁻Na⁺ + NaX (alkyl sodium, a carbanion-like R).
R⁻ then attacks the carbon of a second R–X from the back; X⁻ leaves and a new C–C bond forms: R⁻ + R–X → R–R + X⁻.

blocks.p: Best for **symmetrical alkanes** (R–R, an even number of carbons when R is a straight chain). With two different halides, R–X and R′–X, three alkanes form (R–R, R–R′, R′–R′), which are hard to separate: CH₃Br + C₂H₅Br gives ethane, propane and butane. Methane cannot be made (R–R always has at least two carbons).

list: ✗ Wurtz reaction is done in aqueous solution (it needs dry ether; Na reacts with water).
✗ CH₃Br + C₂H₅Br gives only propane (it gives a mixture of three alkanes).

blocks.p: **Q2.** 2,3-Dimethylbutane: cut the central C–C bond → two isopropyl groups → use 2-bromopropane (isopropyl bromide).

simulation.reason: The idea is a fixed sequence of steps drawn in the video and the notes; there is no continuous variable for a student to explore.
